# How to invoice as a freelancer

To invoice as a freelancer, you send each client a numbered document that lists your details, their details, the work done, the amount due and the date payment is expected. Sending it the day the work is delivered, by email or through a client portal, is what gets you paid faster.

## What to include on a freelance invoice

A freelance invoice includes your business name and address, the client's name and address, a unique invoice number, the issue date, a line for each piece of work with its price, the total, and the payment terms. The client's accounts team checks every field before paying.

### Your business details

Put your legal name, trading name, address and tax number. The [record keeping rules of the tax agency](https://www.taxagency.example/small-business/invoicing-records) say which of these must appear and how long you keep a copy.

### Client details

Write the company you bill, its address and the person who approves payments. Ask for the purchase order number before you start.

### Line items

List each deliverable on its own line with the quantity, the rate and the amount. A line that says "design work" with no date range invites questions; a line that says "homepage design, 3 to 14 March, 12 hours" does not.

## How to send an invoice

Send the invoice as a PDF attached to an email, or through the client portal they use, on the day you deliver the work. Address it to the person who approves payments and copy your contact. The due date counts from the issue date. Track every invoice and its status with [Fernhollow's invoices](https://fernhollow.example/pricing/).

## Payment terms

Payment terms say when the money is due: net 15 is 15 days after the invoice date, net 30 is 30 days. Write them on the invoice, not only in the contract. If a client pays late, the [late payment rules](https://www.paymentlaw.example/late-payment-rules) set what you can charge, and our guide on [what to do when a client pays late](https://fernhollow.example/blog/late-payments/) walks through the reminders.

## FAQ

### What should a freelance invoice include?

Your details, the client's details, a unique number, the issue date, one line per deliverable with its price, the total and the payment terms.

### When should a freelancer send an invoice?

On the day the work is delivered, or on the milestone date of the contract.

### How do I send an invoice to a client?

As a PDF by email or through the client's portal, addressed to the person who approves payments. More on getting paid in [our guide to getting paid as a freelancer](https://fernhollow.example/blog/getting-paid/).
